income_tiers.description: Household size determines income thresholds. Level 1 = highest rebate, Level 3 = lowest (ground-oriented homes only, switching from fossil fuels)
income_tiers.note: Level 3 only applies to ground-oriented homes switching from natural gas, propane, or oil to electric heat pump. Assessed property value ≤$1,230,000.

conditions: Replaces fossil fuel heating (gas, oil, propane) or electric resistance heating
add_ons: Electrical service upgrade: if needed for panel capacity
bc_hydro.process: Pre-register in portal → get code (valid 3 months) → quotes from ESP-registered contractors → contractor receives rebate, homeowner pays remainder

fortisbc.note: FortisBC rebate is flat-rate, not income-qualified. Replaces electric space heating only.
conditions: Replaces electric space heating system with high-efficiency air source heat pump
Replaces electric resistance or gas water heater
Can be added to same ESP application as heat pump

bc_hydro.note: Assessed per home via EnerGuide evaluation. Shrinks the heat pump size needed.

rebate.note: Capped at 50% of total installed cost (labour + materials)

conditions: Licensed contractor with GST + BC licence

rate_change_july_2026.old_rate: Net metering (RS 1289) — closed to new customers June 30, 2026
rate_change_july_2026.old_rate_terms: Excess kWh banked one-for-one at retail rate; annual payout at market price
rate_change_july_2026.new_rate_terms: Excess kWh credited at fixed 10¢/kWh per billing period
rate_change_july_2026.strategy: Size solar to self-consumption, not export. Battery stores midday excess for evening use.
rate_change_july_2026.system_size_limit: Up to 300 kW (vs. 100 kW single-phase before)
rate_change_july_2026.existing_customers: Keep net metering for 10 years from service start; then transition to self-generation rate

bc_hydro.payback_note: Exported kWh = $0.10. Self-consumed kWh = full retail rate. New math makes battery pairing more valuable.

fortisbc.note: FortisBC does not offer a solar rebate. Net metering/self-generation program available; excess generation credited per FortisBC rate schedule.

rebate.note: Peak Saver enrollment must occur within 14 days of interconnection approval. Missing this window = $3,500 cost difference.

peak_saver.how_it_works: BC Hydro briefly adjusts your heating/cooling during peak demand events (winter evenings). You can override anytime.
peak_saver.grid_benefit: Your battery becomes virtual power plant infrastructure; BC Hydro coordinates remotely for grid support.

bc_hydro.eligible_products: CUL 1973 + CUL 9540 certified; commonly used list: https://www.bchydro.com/content/dam/BCHydro/customer-portal/documents/power-smart/residential/programs/energy-storage-battery-list.pdf
bc_hydro.strategy_note: Pairs with solar: store midday excess, use at evening peak (high-value time). Avoids exporting at 10¢/kWh.

offer.timeline: Registration open now; devices ship October 2026

bc_hydro.manufacturer_note: Both Canadian companies. Order through their platforms.
conditions: Register now (email signup), order in October
bc_hydro.eligibility_note: ~40% of BC homes have electric baseboard heat. Program explicitly designed for renters + condos.

bc_hydro.income_note: Household income includes all members 18+, from previous year. Different from ESP table at 5-person threshold.
bc_hydro.renter_note: Yes, if utility account is in renter's name (not landlord/strata).
bc_hydro.reorder: Allowed after 5 years or after moving
bc_hydro.utility_note: Program brought to you by BC Hydro, FortisBC, Pacific Natural Gas — renters in any service area can apply

bc_hydro.availability: First-come, first-served, subject to available funding
bc_hydro.note: Program expanded June 29, 2026 to include MORE low-income homeowners AND tenants. See expanded program details.

charger_requirements: Must be on official BC Hydro eligible list
NACS J3400 or SAE J1772 connector
bc_hydro.electrical_permit: Required (contractor pulls it; Technical Safety BC or municipality)
gotchas: Rebate NOT available for 240V outlet installation only
Pre-existing 240V outlet = simplified application (charger invoice + photo), zero electrical work
Submit rebate docs within 90 days of installation (some sources say 180 days — link both, advise applying immediately)
bc_hydro.local_municipal_topups: Some cities offer additional rebates — research per city
bc_hydro.eligible_charger_list_note: Do not replicate this list — it changes. Link with verified-date stamp.

renter_paths.description: Renters can qualify for several programs, depending on utility account ownership and income
eligible_programs: free_energy_saving_kit (if income-qualified + utility account in renter's name)
renter_paths.heat_pump_note: Renters can apply for ESP heat pump rebates with landlord consent form. Utility account must not be in landlord/strata name.
free_offerings: 5 free smart thermostats (up to $350 value, October 2026, baseboard heat only)
Free energy saving kit (income-qualified, 3–6 weeks delivery)
Free retrofit program (ECAP, income-qualified, expanded June 2026)

condo_paths.description: Condos/apartments historically excluded from heat pump rebates in BC. This has changed as of July 2026.
eligible_programs: heat_pump ($5,000 if electrically heated, vs. $16K ground-oriented homes)
condo_paths.heat_pump_note: Condos with electric baseboard or resistance heating qualify for up to $5,000 heat pump rebate. NOT $16K, but significant.
condo_paths.solar_battery_note: Strata units, secondary suites, separately metered units NOT eligible for solar/battery rebates.
condo_paths.provincial_note: Ontario differs — condos fully ineligible there.

utility_routing.description: Different utilities route to different programs

fortisbc.note: FortisBC does not offer solar/battery rebates. Uses self-generation rate instead.

july_1_solar_rate_change.old: Net metering (RS 1289) closed to new customers
july_1_solar_rate_change.impact: Sizing strategy shifts to self-consumption + battery pairing

july_6_smart_thermostat_launch.new_program: Free smart thermostats via Power Smart 2.0
july_6_smart_thermostat_launch.target: 800,000 BC homes with electric baseboard heat
